contamination.detail: NOT a blind read. 1-048 is one of the two pages that predate this pipeline; gt/ocr/chukchi-1-048.xml already held hand-keyed text and I read it (via `harness lines`) before reading the raster. This is a revision pass, so the proposal is that text as re-checked against the 300 dpi scan, not an independent reading. Treat agreement between proposal and existing GT as weak evidence: on any line I did not flag, the two witnesses are not independent.

27.resolved: Wuˊkwên = W, u, U+02CA, k, w, e+U+0302, n

28.text: inhabitants afterwards turned to reindeér-breeding and went inland.
28.resolved: reindeér = r, e, i, n, d, e, U+0301 COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT, r
28.note: CHANGED from GT 'reindeer-breeding'. FOR THE ADJUDICATOR — this is the one reading on the page I cannot settle myself, and it is an editorial call, not an optical one. The print carries an acute over the second 'e' of 'reindeer'. At 4x (zoom4-002.png, strip 28.5) it is a solid tapered wedge at type weight and slant, identical in form to the stress sorts elsewhere on the page, and categorically unlike the round artifact dots this page is littered with (see line 46). So it is ink from this forme, not a speck and not show-through. But 'reindeér' is not a word, this is English prose, and U+0301 is catalogued nowhere in keying_spec — it would be the corpus's first combining acute. Read as a foul-case sort: the compositor set an accented 'e'. Keyed as printed per §1 ('keying reproduces print') and the readings.md MISPRINT habit, flagged rather than silently corrected to 'reindeer' or silently dropped. If the editor rules it a defect rather than a reading, delete the mark here — but the ruling should be recorded, because nothing mechanical will catch this again.

46.resolved: Kihiˊni = K, i, h, i, U+02CA, n, i (twice)
46.note: UNCHANGED from GT, but the ruling is worth recording. The print sets a raised mark after the FIRST Kihi-stress-ni (before "Island") which the second occurrence does not carry. At 4x (zoom4-004.png, strip 46.4) it is a small ROUND dot, plainly distinct from the slanted tapered wedge of the stress mark in the same word. Not keyed, for two independent reasons. (a) This page carries dozens of identical raised round dots over ordinary English words - after "Only" (line 6), "villages" (10), "desert" and "according" (11), "families," (33), "outward" (42) - and this mark belongs to that population, which is a page-wide print or show-through artifact rather than a sort. (b) The only round raised sort in the inventory is U+02D9, licensed by keying_spec 2.1 only after n x d t s c-caron j-caron; this one follows i, so keying it would assert a sequence the notation does not contain. Overrule if the editor reads it as ink.
